messages:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up re: continuous-batcher + queue topology. Flatten lanes boosted throughput for small reqs but we saw tenant tail spikes and KV-cache churn. Want to capture tradeoffs and pick an experiment path.

ashwin: where did you run this and can you paste the repro config?

maria: hosted (dev-staging g4dn). Repro (condensed):
```
scripts/load_test --tenants 50 --mix small:0.7,large:0.3 --dur 20m
batcher.topology=flat
batcher.slice_residency=4
batcher.quanta_ceiling=128
```
Outcome: tokens/sec +12% but 3 tenants hit >500ms tail; their KV miss rate spiked.

kevin: flattening reduces packing inefficiencies but increases contention for residency slots. Two levers: (1) queue-striping (tenant -> micro-lane) or (2) handoff-token leases to bound eviction storms.

jen: eviction churn implies some tenants lose warm prefixes between windows. Are we seeing long gaps for those tenants?

praveen: I have a handoff-token proto sketch: small lease given to a tenant slice to hold residency for N quanta. Pseudo: HandoffToken {tenant_id, lease_expiry_ms, allowed_quanta, reentrant}. When held, preemptions wait or require revoke. Pros: bounds KV churn for token holder. Cons: can hog resources.

ashwin: tradeoffs look clear: token reduces tail for holder but may raise P99 for others. Combine with striping so tokens are scoped to micro-lane to limit global impact.

sam: observability gap: we need slice_continuous_residency metrics. Propose gauges: current_residency_quanta, last_eviction_reason, kv_cache_miss_rate_per_tenant. Also trace accumulated_quanta per-slice.

kevin: +1 on trace span for accumulated_quanta to correlate with kv misses offline.

jen: softer alternative: soft-residency boost based on recent kv-hit-rate; e.g., if hit_rate > .8, give extra_quanta for next X quanta. Less heavy-handed than hard leases.

maria: options: A) stripe + soft-residency boost (lower risk), B) flat + handoff-token (stronger guarantee). I prefer A first.

praveen: experiment proto for A: lane_count L, per-tenant lane = hash(tenant_id)%L, soft_boost: {threshold:.8, extra_quanta:2, decay_sec:30}. Runtime changes: lane mapping + boost check on admission.

ashwin: choose L carefully (power of two). 16 vs 64 tradeoff: more lanes reduce tenant collisions but add scheduling overhead.

sam: propose experiment matrix: L in {8,32}, slice_residency in {3,6}, soft_extra_quanta in {1,2}. Run 2h each with synthetic and replayed traces. Capture p50/p95/p99, kv-miss, tokens/sec, per-tenant kv-warmth.

kevin: also add per-lane max-sustained-quanta-per-window (circuit-breaker) to prevent long domination.

maria: action items: (maria) draft experiment PR + harness; (sam) add metrics & span; (praveen) refine handoff-token for RFC followup; (ashwin/kevin) run matrix and analyze.

jen: :thumbsup: add a dedicated canary with reserved tenant on Dedicated to validate predictability for enterprise customers.

runtime-bot: deploybot: ci/presubmit passed for batcher-refactor-experiment branch (build #4821).

maria: I'll post the PR link here when ready. One more idea from ashwin: compute a cheap \"kv-warmth\" metric = fraction of prefixes with recent hits and use that for affinity heuristics. Filing as instrumentation TODO. End thread for now.
